project.title: Typer Inner Checker
project.display_title: Typer Inner Checker — Locomotive BASIC listing validator
project.status: Primary source and development transcript reviewed; independent browser execution not performed

evidence: The checked-in Claude-discussion.txt transcript records Brett's requests and Claude's implementation, extension and test descriptions for the tool.

identity.narrative: The monorepo root identifies Typer Inner Checker as a browser page for checking Locomotive BASIC program listings, and the directory contains the self-contained implementation.

classification.narrative: This is modern retro-development tooling: it validates source listings, recognizes BASIC vocabulary, checks line structure and references, and supports listing load/save; it is not an emulator and does not execute programs.

source_cpu.narrative: The tool analyzes textual Locomotive BASIC listings rather than an original machine-code binary, so assigning the CPC's processor as a recovered source CPU would be misleading.

target_cpu.narrative: The output is normalized BASIC text and saved BAS files, not a native CPU-targeted port or reconstructed binary.

build.narrative: The inspected artifact is a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript page. No browser execution or functional test was performed in this pass, so build and runnable flags remain unknown.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed material says the page opens in a browser but gives no minimum CPU, RAM, browser or operating-system requirement suitable for a runtime profile.

ai.narrative: The repository preserves a detailed Brett/Claude development transcript in which Claude states that it built, extended and tested the checker; this is explicit project-specific AI contribution evidence.

relationships.narrative: Typer Inner Checker is a separate titled tool inside BrettHallen/Amstrad-CPC. It supports transcribing CPC listings and is distinct from the repository's Laserwarp analysis and hardware subprojects.

project.title: Atari Jaguar 240p Test Suite
project.display_title: 240p Test Suite — Atari Jaguar native diagnostics
project.status: Active Jaguar fork with v0.x releases; primary source reviewed, independent build/run not performed

identity.narrative: The project identifies itself as the Atari Jaguar 240p Test Suite, a bare-metal port of Artemio Urbina's diagnostic suite with Jaguar-specific tests and tagged pre-1.0 releases.

classification.narrative: This is substantial original homebrew porting work, not reverse engineering: it implements calibration patterns, lag/audio tests and Jaguar hardware probes as native console software.

source_cpu.narrative: The port is derived from the high-level 240p Test Suite project rather than recovery of an original machine-code binary, so no predecessor CPU is assigned.

target_cpu.narrative: The build documentation explicitly requires m68k-atari-mint cross tools and produces Atari Jaguar ROM formats, establishing the native m68k output architecture without asserting a minimum runtime CPU.

build.narrative: The README documents Docker and native toolchain paths, multiple ROM formats, releases and emulator smoke tests. No build, ROM execution or real-hardware test was independently performed, so boolean build/run flags remain unknown.

runtime_profiles.narrative: Native Atari Jaguar execution and cartridge/emulator loading routes are documented, but no variant-specific minimum CPU/RAM profile beyond the target console was established.

ai.narrative: The repository contains agent-configuration files, but those are not contribution evidence; the reviewed README and primary project material do not explicitly attribute implementation to an AI tool, so usage remains unknown.

relationships.narrative: The README identifies JoeMatt's project as an active fork of BitJag's original Jaguar port and as a port of Artemio Urbina's broader 240p Test Suite. BitJag and ArtemioUrbina Jaguar repositories are recorded as lineage duplicates, not independent projects.

project.title: JagLBA
project.display_title: JagLBA — Little Big Adventure source port for Atari Jaguar
project.status: Work in progress; first room and scripts run in BigPEmu, earlier renderer tested on real Jaguar; far from playable

identity.narrative: JagLBA identifies itself as a 6 MB Atari Jaguar cartridge port of Little Big Adventure, built from the released GPL engine source and requiring user-supplied game data.

classification.narrative: This is a source-derived native port, not a binary-derived reconstruction. The current project is explicitly far from playable; the first room, scripts and interaction run in BigPEmu, while an earlier renderer-only build was tested on real hardware.

source_cpu.narrative: The input is a released C engine lineage with formerly x86 assembly modules translated to C, not recovery from a specific original executable, so an original binary CPU is not assigned.

target_cpu.narrative: The README explicitly says the engine runs on the Jaguar's 68000 and describes GPU rendering plus DSP audio work; the repository contains 68000 boot/interrupt code and GPU/DSP kernels.

build.narrative: The Windows build path requires owned LBA data, Python, Docker with a documented m68k toolchain image, RMAC and Jaguar SDK headers, and writes separate emulator and hardware ROMs. No build or execution was independently performed.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The documentation establishes Atari Jaguar and BigPEmu execution paths and a 6 MB cartridge image, but it does not provide a variant minimum CPU/RAM profile beyond the console target.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI attribution was established in the reviewed README and provenance document; absence is recorded as unknown rather than non-use.

relationships.narrative: The provenance file records a direct chain from lba1-classic-community through PSX-LBA and DS-LBA, with selected HS-LBA fixes. These are source-port predecessors, not evidence of Jaguar binary reverse engineering.

project.title: jaguarcartreader
project.display_title: Jaguar Cartridge Reader — 16-bit dump and bus-analysis firmware
source_language: Atari Jaguar cartridge ROM and bus data
project.status: Primary firmware and documentation reviewed; independent hardware execution not performed

identity.narrative: Tolbat's jaguarcartreader is a modified standalone Atari Jaguar cartridge-reader firmware with 4 MB and 6 MB 16-bit dump modes and a read-only cartridge analyzer.

classification.narrative: This qualifies as preservation and binary-analysis tooling: it measures cartridge bus behavior, samples address ranges and output-enable states, checks read stability, and writes standard J64 images. It is not a reverse-engineered game or a general hardware project record.

source_cpu.narrative: The tool dumps cartridge ROM bytes and characterizes the physical data-bus layout without interpreting a specific game's executable CPU instructions, so no original CPU is assigned.

target_cpu.narrative: The reviewed fork documents Arduino IDE and library dependencies but does not explicitly identify a processor model in its own primary material; no firmware CPU is inferred from the hardware family.

build.narrative: The README lists Arduino IDE 1.8.19 and pinned display/storage libraries, and the repository contains the Arduino firmware. The firmware was not compiled, flashed or run on reader hardware in this pass.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed fork does not provide a complete minimum hardware profile for the standalone reader, so no CPU/RAM/chipset runtime profile is recorded.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI attribution was found in the reviewed README or firmware header; usage remains unknown.

relationships.narrative: The README identifies Tolbat's work as a modification of PsychoFox11/GrumpyGopher/sakman55 reader lineage. The OSCR User Group fork carries the same analyzer and 16-bit modes with build/release automation, so it is recorded as a duplicate successor rather than a separate project.
